Expectation: Apply the Guidelines in proportion to the institution's size and activities and to the risk materiality of each AI use case

Basic governance where an AI failure is unlikely to have a material impact: a named senior manager, permitted and prohibited uses, human review of outputs, an approved list of AI tools, staff education, compliance checks and periodic review
The board approves and reviews the governance approach for AI risk, addresses AI in the risk appetite framework and understands AI well enough to challenge
What the wiki does not cover: No control or test case covers board understanding of AI or quantitative risk appetite measures

Expectation: Senior management implements the framework, assigns roles across business lines and control functions, escalates AI incidents and threshold breaches, and resources AI risk management
Local senior management stays accountable where a group framework is used
What the wiki does not cover: The wiki does not address group and local accountability

Expectation: Identify AI use consistently across the institution, including AI inside third-party services and shadow AI, under a designated control function
Keep an accurate AI inventory with key attributes, linked to other inventories, with agent-specific attributes where relevant
Assess the risk materiality of each use case on impact, complexity and reliance, before and after controls, with a control function approving the rating
Contingency plans and fallback for high-risk use cases, and tested activation of kill switches
Data management: fitness for purpose, representativeness, quality, classification, security, privacy, and auditability and lineage
Transparency and explainability matched to the use case and its audience, with customer notice and redress for high-impact decisions
Define fair outcomes, run fairness assessments that consider protected attributes and their proxies, and document mitigation
Human oversight: assigned roles, competent overseers with authority to intervene, design that supports oversight, and review of interventions and near misses
Third-party AI: test it in the institution's own context, secure contractual visibility of changes, assess the supply chain and concentration risk, plan for failure and keep a right to audit
Document why an AI system, model or feature was selected over simpler alternatives
What the wiki does not cover: No control covers the rationale for selecting a model or feature

Expectation: Evaluation and testing against measurable thresholds, including stress, adversarial and sub-population tests; guardrails for known limitations; failure modes of generative AI and AI agents
What the wiki does not cover: Overfitting mitigation and statistical validation methods are outside the wiki

Expectation: Technology and cybersecurity controls: secured environments, access control and separation of duties, and governance of third-party components
Document development so that an independent party can understand and reproduce it
Review before deployment by people not involved in development, formal independent validation for high-risk use cases, and findings reported to the approval body
What the wiki does not cover: The wiki gates release on a security review. It has no control on independent model validation

Expectation: Technology and cybersecurity review before go-live: secure design, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, red teaming and tests against adversarial threats
Ongoing monitoring with metrics and thresholds, drift checks, AI incident and issue management, user feedback, and logging of prompts and responses for generative AI and agents
Re-validation and review, regular for high-risk use cases and when triggered by changes, alerts or new risks
Change management: a way to judge how significant a change is, re-approval, version control with rollback, and tighter controls for automatic updates
Retirement and decommissioning of AI
Competence and conduct of the people who develop, deploy and use AI, with regular review of capability and capacity
Technology infrastructure adequate for performance, scalability and resilience
